title: Microsoft AI finishes pre-training MAI-Base-2, a 2.8T MoE foundation model
subtitle: A lab post on October 15 says the 80B-active mixture-of-experts was trained on 16,000 GB200s over 38 days and claims 4-12x the pre-training FLOPs efficiency of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base; weights are not yet released.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Microsoft AI announced on October 15 that it has completed pre-training on MAI-Base-2, the first in-house base model from Mustafa Suleyman's MAI Superintelligence team at frontier scale. Per the lab post relayed by Yahoo Finance and Street Insider, the model is a mixture-of-experts with roughly 2.8 trillion total parameters and 80 billion active per token, routing each token to 7 of 512 experts plus 1 shared expert. Training ran on 16,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs over 38 days across August and September 2026, with a corpus near 50 trillion tokens and about 18% vision-language data. The model is still in post-training; there is no public API, no agent benchmark, and no release date. Microsoft says it plans to license weights to trusted partners via Foundry.

The headline figure is efficiency, not raw size. Microsoft claims MAI-Base-2 is 4 to 12 times more pre-training FLOPs-efficient than DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base (sources give the range as 4.2 to 12.3x). The company attributes most of the gain to fixes in its MoE implementation, saying utilization of the MoE layer rose from 24% to 35%, with the rest coming from data mix and routing. These are Microsoft's own numbers; no third party has yet replicated them, and the base model has not been evaluated against public benchmarks that an outside team could score.

The strategic subtext is familiar. Microsoft's revised OpenAI agreement from April 2026 removed the clauses that had kept it from training frontier models independently; the April MAI-Transcribe/Voice/Image launches, the June MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model, and the Ali Farhadi / ex-Ai2 hiring run through the summer all pointed toward exactly this moment — a self-trained Microsoft base model at a scale that no longer depends on OpenAI's pre-training stack. Shipping only via Foundry, to trusted partners, mirrors how OpenAI and Anthropic handle their own frontier bases: the weights don't need to be open to shift Microsoft's position inside the Azure stack.

For learners: a base model is not a product. What Microsoft announced is the raw pre-trained weights before any instruction tuning, RLHF, or safety work — the layer that other labs usually keep private. The 'MAI-Thinking-1' reasoning model you can actually call in Foundry today sits on top of a base like this one; the base is what decides the ceiling that post-training can reach. When you see claims about pre-training FLOPs efficiency, the useful question is not 'is 10x true?' — it is 'measured against what, on what hardware, with what data budget.' Those three variables control almost every number in a modern frontier announcement.
